Patched only in glob 14.0.2 (published 2026-10-27T22:07Z; the seven-day rule admits it from 2026-11-03T22:07Z), a new major for every consumer here. The advisory matches glob >=9.0.0 <=14.0.1, so only glob 13.0.6 (node_modules/glob) is affected; the glob 7.2.3 copies under jest are outside that range and are flagged only through their minimatch ^3 dependency (see GHSA-g3hv-75wg-m249). glob 13.0.6 is reached only through @nestjs/cli (a devDependency, pinned there exactly as glob 13.0.6), which runs `nest build`; `npm prune --omit=dev` leaves it out of the production image. The bypass keeps walking after an AbortSignal fires, and nothing here passes an AbortSignal or a request-supplied pattern to glob, so the surface is the build's own patterns on this repository's own files. The later bump has to settle whether glob 14.0.2 can be forced under @nestjs/cli with an override: the pin is exact, and @nestjs/cli 12.0.11 (npm's suggested fix) drops glob but needs TypeScript 6 and pins minimatch 10.2.6, which is still in range. Re-check with `npm view @nestjs/cli@latest dependencies`. Remove when glob 14.0.2 or newer is locked.

Patched only in minimatch 11.0.1 (published 2026-10-27T22:26Z; the seven-day rule admits it from 2026-11-03T22:26Z). The advisory marks every release below 11.0.1 vulnerable, so no release inside the ^3 or ^10 lines the consumers declare is patched. Two copies, both dev-only and absent from the production image: 10.2.5 (glob 13.0.6, ^10.2.2) and 3.1.5 (fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin 9.1.0 under @nestjs/cli, test-exclude 6.0.0 under jest's coverage, and glob 7.2.3 under jest, all ^3). They match this repository's own glob patterns at build and test time; no request-supplied pattern reaches them, so the globparts amplification has no exposed surface. The later bump has to settle each copy on its own. 10.2.5 can take an override to 11.0.1 if it lands with glob 14.0.2 (which wants ^11.0.0). The 3.1.5 copies cannot take one as they stand: test-exclude 6 and fork-ts-checker-webpack-plugin 9 call the module itself as a function, and minimatch 11 only has named exports, so they pin an old major with no patched release in its line and stay flagged until jest and Nest move off them (test-exclude 8.0.0 still declares ^10.2.2). If they cannot move by the expiry, renew this entry with that reason rather than forcing the override. Re-check with `npm ls minimatch --package-lock-only`.

Patched in node-forge 1.4.1 (published 2026-10-27T04:44Z) and 1.4.2 (2026-10-27T14:09Z); the seven-day rule admits 1.4.2 from 2026-11-03T14:09Z, so today the patch is only too young. The bump is a plain lockfile refresh: both consumers declare a range that already takes it (@expo/cli ^1.3.3 and @expo/code-signing-certificates ^1.3.3), so no override is needed. node-forge is pulled in by expo's development tooling only, @expo/cli (the dev server and CLI) and the code-signing helper it uses, and is not imported by the application bundle. Checked in the published sources of @expo/cli 56.1.19 and @expo/code-signing-certificates 0.0.6: they call only forge.pki (certificate and key creation and parsing, such as certificateFromPem on the developer's own keychain certificate in `expo run:ios`), forge.md.sha256, forge.util and forge.random. The PEM decoder therefore only sees the developer's own certificates, on the developer's machine or in EAS Build; the ReDoS has no attacker-supplied input here. Delete this entry together with the other node-forge entries when the bump lands, including GHSA-86w9-cpqp-85rv, whose 'no patched release' reason no longer holds. Re-check with `npm ls node-forge --package-lock-only` in mobile/.
